chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Main Types of Real Estate

lessons.title: Commercial Property: Offices, Retail and Warehousing

children.text: Dr Kavita Joshi, a dentist in Pune, owns a 2BHK in Aundh that earns about 3% a year in rent. Her CA suggests an office unit in Baner, already rented to a private bank, yielding 8%. "Why would anyone buy a flat when an office pays almost three times more?" she asks. It is the right question. The answer is that the extra rent is not free money. It is payment for risks that residential property does not carry. This lesson shows you what those risks are across offices, retail and warehousing.

body.text: Commercial property pays higher rent because your tenant is a business, and businesses relocate, downsize and shut down. A higher yield is the price of vacancy risk, bigger tickets and more complex ownership.

children.text: That last row matters most. A flat's price is set largely by what families will pay to live in it. A commercial property's price is set almost entirely by the rent it earns. No tenant, no income, and very few buyers.
Offices: Grade A Parks vs Strata Units

markDefs.definition: High-quality office buildings with large floor plates, modern building systems, professional management and reputed tenants, typically owned by institutions or REITs.
An office building sold floor by floor or unit by unit to many individual owners, rather than held by one owner.

children.text: India's office market splits into two worlds.
Grade A

business parks like those along Bengaluru's Outer Ring Road or in Mumbai's BKC are usually owned whole by developers, institutions or REITs, and leased to global companies. Individual investors mostly buy into
strata-sold offices

, where a building is divided among dozens of owners. Strata units are affordable, but a building with many owners often struggles with maintenance, upgrades and attracting large tenants who want whole floors.

children.text: How a Commercial Lease Works
Tenure.
Office leases in India commonly run for 9 years, structured as 3 + 3 + 3, with the tenant able to exit at the end of each block.

markDefs.definition: The period at the start of a lease during which the tenant cannot leave without paying the rent for the remaining lock-in months.

children.text: Lock-in.
The
lock-in period
, often the first 3 years, is the only stretch where your income is contractually secure.
Escalation.
Rent rises by a fixed amount written into the lease, commonly 15% every 3 years or around 5% a year.
Security deposit.
Tenants typically pay several months of rent upfront as a refundable deposit.

markDefs.definition: Common Area Maintenance: charges for security, cleaning, lifts, power backup and upkeep of shared spaces in a commercial building.

children.text: Running costs.
The tenant usually pays
CAM charges
while occupying the space. When the unit is empty, the owner pays them.

Back to Dr Joshi's Baner office: price ₹1.2 crore, rent ₹80,000 a month, 9-year lease with 15% escalation every 3 years. Gross yield in year one is ₹9,60,000 ÷ ₹1,20,00,000 = 8%. If the bank stays for all nine years, here is how the rent grows:

body.title: Annual rent on the Baner office with 15% escalation every 3 years (₹ lakh)

children.text: Years 4 to 6: ₹80,000 × 1.15 = ₹92,000 a month, or ₹11,04,000 a year and ₹33,12,000 in total
Nine-year total: ₹28,80,000 + ₹33,12,000 + ₹38,08,800 = ₹1,00,00,800, about 83% of the ₹1.2 crore purchase price, before tax and costs

body.title: The first escalation
body.prompt: The Baner office rents for ₹80,000 a month, with a 15% escalation after year 3. What is the monthly rent in year 4, in ₹?
body.explanation: ₹80,000 × 1.15 = ₹92,000 a month. Built-in escalations are one of the most attractive features of a commercial lease, but they only pay out if the tenant actually stays.

children.text: The Risk Behind the Yield: Vacancy

body.caption: Owner's costs include property tax, and CAM charges for any months the unit sits empty.

body.title: A bad year
body.prompt: The bank leaves the ₹1.2 crore Baner office at the end of a lock-in. In the following year, the unit earns ₹80,000 a month for only 4 months and sits empty for 8 months, during which the owner pays ₹12,000 a month in CAM charges. What is the net yield for that year, in %? Round to two decimal places.
body.explanation: Rent received: 4 × ₹80,000 = ₹3,20,000. CAM paid while empty: 8 × ₹12,000 = ₹96,000. Net: ₹2,24,000 ÷ ₹1,20,00,000 = 1.87%. One tenant exit turned an 8% asset into a sub-2% asset for the year, worse than the flat Dr Joshi already owns.

body.text: Be very careful with "assured return" and "pre-leased" pitches. An assured return from a developer is only as good as the developer's finances, and many NCR strata projects that promised 10% to 12% stopped paying. A pre-leased unit is only as good as the tenant and the lease: check who the tenant is, how long the lock-in runs, and what happens when it ends.

children.text: Retail: Malls, High Streets and Shops

markDefs.definition: A lease where the tenant pays a minimum fixed rent or a percentage of its store sales, whichever is higher.

children.text: Retail property earns money from shoppers' footfall. Well-run Grade A malls, like those owned by Phoenix Mills or Nexus Select Trust, are held by a single owner who controls the brand mix and marketing. Their leases often include a
revenue share

, so the owner earns more when stores sell more. The problem for individual investors is that the malls they can buy into are usually strata-sold malls, where hundreds of owners each hold a shop. Nobody controls the tenant mix, footfall drops, and the mall slowly empties. Many such "dead malls" dot the NCR and other cities.

body.label: Grade A mall vacancy in India
body.context: Q1 2026, with Grade A+ malls at just 2.6%. Quality malls are scarce and full; weaker, strata-sold malls can have far higher vacancy.

children.text: Warehousing: The Quiet Winner

markDefs.definition: Third-party logistics: companies that store, pack and deliver goods on behalf of other businesses.

children.text: Every Flipkart order, Blinkit delivery and FMCG shipment passes through a warehouse. Rising e-commerce, quick commerce and manufacturing have made warehousing one of the fastest-growing commercial segments, in logistics hubs like Bhiwandi near Mumbai, Chakan near Pune, Hoskote near Bengaluru and the Delhi-NCR belt. The biggest tenants are
3PL

firms and e-commerce players. Large, modern warehouse parks are almost entirely built and owned by institutional platforms, so individuals typically access this segment through listed companies, REITs or funds rather than direct ownership.

body.text: Commercial property is where REITs make the strongest case. A single ₹1.2 crore strata office puts all your money on one tenant. An office REIT unit spreads the same rupee across millions of square feet and hundreds of tenants in Grade A parks you could never buy directly. You will study REITs properly in Chapter 5.

body.title: Why the higher yield?
body.question: Why does a pre-leased office unit usually offer a higher rental yield than a flat of the same price in the same city?
options: Offices always appreciate faster than flats
Investors demand extra return for longer vacancies, tenant concentration and a smaller pool of buyers
Commercial tenants never leave before the lease ends
body.explanation: The higher yield compensates for real risks: a business tenant can leave after the lock-in, re-letting can take many months, and fewer buyers exist when you sell. Commercial property does not reliably appreciate faster than residential.

body.title: Name the clause
body.textWithBlank: A lease clause that automatically raises rent by 15% every three years is called an ___ clause.
body.explanation: Escalation clauses build rent growth into commercial leases. They make income more predictable, as long as the tenant stays past the lock-in.

body.title: The 12% assured return food court
body.scenario: Suresh, a retired PSU officer in Ghaziabad, is offered a 300 sq ft food court unit in an under-construction strata mall in Greater Noida for ₹45 lakh. The developer promises a 12% "assured return" for 3 years until the mall opens, after which the unit will be "leased to leading brands."
body.prompt: What questions and risks should Suresh consider before investing?
body.modelAnswer:
1. Who pays the 12%: an assured return is paid by the developer, not a tenant. If the developer's finances weaken, payments can stop. Suresh should check the developer's track record and RERA history.
2. Is the return already in the price: a unit priced well above comparable space may simply be refunding part of Suresh's own money back to him.
3. Strata mall risk: hundreds of owners, no single controller of the brand mix. Upper-floor food courts in weaker malls often struggle for footfall and tenants.
4. After year 3: there is no signed tenant, so there is no guaranteed income once the assured period ends.
5. Liquidity: Suresh cannot easily sell a 300 sq ft food court unit if he needs the money, especially if the mall underperforms.
6. Concentration and suitability: ₹45 lakh in one illiquid, untenanted unit may be a large share of a retiree's savings.
7. Alternatives: a retail or office REIT offers exposure to leased, operating assets with daily liquidity and regular distributions.

body.title: Before Buying Any Commercial Unit
steps: Identify the tenant and check its financial strength
Read the lease: tenure, lock-in, escalation, deposit and exit clauses
Ask how long similar units in the building have stayed vacant
Confirm who pays CAM charges and property tax, and when
Check whether the building is single-owner or strata-sold, and how well it is maintained
Compare the yield with an office or retail REIT's distribution yield

cards.definition: A high-quality, professionally managed office building leased to reputed tenants, usually held by one owner or a REIT.
A building divided and sold unit by unit to many owners.
The part of a lease during which the tenant cannot exit without paying for the remaining period.
A pre-agreed rent increase, such as 15% every three years.
Common Area Maintenance charges for shared services in a commercial building, paid by the owner when the unit is vacant.
A retail lease where the tenant pays the higher of a fixed minimum rent or a share of store sales.
Third-party logistics firms that store and move goods for other businesses; the largest warehouse tenants in India.

points: Commercial property yields more than residential because business tenants bring vacancy risk, longer re-letting periods and fewer buyers.
Offices split into institution-owned Grade A parks and strata-sold units; individuals mostly access the weaker second category directly.
Leases add structure: 3 + 3 + 3 tenure, lock-ins and escalations like 15% every three years.
One tenant exit can crush a year's return, as when an 8% office fell to 1.87% in our example.
Single-owner Grade A malls thrive, while many strata-sold malls struggle; treat assured-return pitches with deep suspicion.
Warehousing is booming on 3PL and e-commerce demand, but is mostly accessible through REITs, listed companies and funds.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not investment, tax or legal advice. Yields, lease terms, GST treatment and vacancy vary by property, city and tenant. Companies and REITs are named as examples, not recommendations. Consult a SEBI-registered investment adviser and a qualified tax professional before making investment decisions.
